liebermann.notes: Once part of the Liber custumarum of the London Guildhall, written c. 1310 with coloured decoration; one of the manuscripts of the Leges Anglorum s. XIII in Londoniis collectae: Quadripartitus laws with London inventions (ff. 2–17), Tripartita with the London interpolation (ff. 30–40), Genealogia Normannica; f. 41 (K3, 15th c.) copies Sc (Wl art retr, Wl lad, CHn cor, Hn mon, Hn com, Concordia of 1153); f. 43 Hn with CHn cor and Hn Lond. In the 17th century Harley 311 (Hn) was collated with it and Additional 16278 copied Ine to Cnut from it; Cambridge Trinity O 10, 20 used both parts.

entries.text_de:
Cotton Claudius D II, einst ein Theil des Liber custumarum der Londoner Guildhall8, geschrieben um 1310 mit farbigem Schmuck, ist einer der Codices der Leges Anglorum s. XIII. in. Londoniis collectae; s. u. Lond. Fol. 1 Numerus prouinciarum, hidarum9. [Vorher ging Expositio uocabulorum.10]

F. 2—17 aus Quadripartitus mit eingefügten historischen Bindegliedern und scheinbar gesetzgeberischen Stücken Londoner Erfindung. F. 2 Ine, u. S. 89; f. 4b Blas, Forf, u. S. 389; Hu, u. S. 192; f. 5 Af von Einl. 49, 9 an, u. S. 47; f. 8 AGu, u. S. 127; f. 8b App. AGu, u. S. 394; EGu, u. S. 129; f. 10 I As, As Alm, II As, u. S. 147 f. 151; f. 12 Episc, u. S. 477; Norðleod, Mirce; f. 12b Að, Had, u. S. 459—65; f. 12b IV. V As, f. 13b III. VI As, u. S. 171. 167. 170. 173; f. 15b Ordal, u. S. 386; f. 17—24b Cnut, u. S. 279.

F. 30—40 aus Tripartita: Rubriken zu Wl art retr und ECf retr; f. 31 Wl art retr, u. S. 489: ein Blatt davon ist ausgerissen, s. u. S. 49137; f. 31 ECf retr, Lond interpol., u. S. 627; f. 40b Geneal. Normannica.

Später eingefügt und im 15. Jh. geschrieben ist f. 41, das ich K 3 nenne, mit Copie der Blätter Sc f. 162 ff. (vgl. unten), nämlich Wl art retr, u. S. 489; Wl lad aus Quadr., u. S. 483; CHn cor, u. S. 521; Hn mon, u. S. 523; Hn com, u. S. 524; Concordia inter Stephanum et Henricum [1153].

F. 43 Hn, u. S. 547, mit CHn cor und Hn Ld.

Hieraus collationirte im 17. Jh. Hn Harley 311 und copirte Ine bis Cnut Additional 16278. Beide Theile benutzte Cambr. Trin. O 10, 20.
entries.text_en:
Cotton Claudius D II, formerly part of the Liber custumarum of the London Guildhall8, written c. 1310 with coloured decoration, is one of the codices of the Leges Anglorum s. XIII. in. Londoniis collectae; see below, Lond. Fol. 1 Numerus prouinciarum, hidarum9. [Before it came Expositio uocabulorum.10]

F. 2—17 from Quadripartitus, with inserted historical connecting links and pieces of London invention that pass for legislation. F. 2 Ine, below, p. 89; f. 4b Blas, Forf, below, p. 389; Hu, below, p. 192; f. 5 Af from Introduction 49, 9 on, below, p. 47; f. 8 AGu, below, p. 127; f. 8b App. AGu, below, p. 394; EGu, below, p. 129; f. 10 I As, As Alm, II As, below, p. 147 f. 151; f. 12 Episc, below, p. 477; Norðleod, Mirce; f. 12b Að, Had, below, pp. 459—65; f. 12b IV. V As, f. 13b III. VI As, below, pp. 171. 167. 170. 173; f. 15b Ordal, below, p. 386; f. 17—24b Cnut, below, p. 279.

F. 30—40 from Tripartita: rubrics to Wl art retr and ECf retr; f. 31 Wl art retr, below, p. 489: one leaf of it has been torn out, see below, p. 49137; f. 31 ECf retr, Lond interpol., below, p. 627; f. 40b Geneal. Normannica.

Inserted later and written in the 15th century is f. 41, which I call K 3, with a copy of the leaves Sc f. 162 ff. (cf. below), namely Wl art retr, below, p. 489; Wl lad from Quadr., below, p. 483; CHn cor, below, p. 521; Hn mon, below, p. 523; Hn com, below, p. 524; Concordia inter Stephanum et Henricum [1153].

F. 43 Hn, below, p. 547, with CHn cor and Hn Ld.

From this, in the 17th century, Harley 311 collated Hn, and Additional 16278 copied Ine to Cnut. Both parts were used by Cambr. Trin. O 10, 20.

transcription.doubts: Heading: 'K 2' and 'K 3' bold, '(oder K)' with K in roman. The entry runs from the foot of column 1 to column 2 of the same page. 'u. S. 147 f. 151' as printed (probably 'pp. 147 f., 151'). 'f. 31' is printed twice (for Wl art retr and ECf retr). 'u. S. 491<sup>37</sup>': superscript 37 refers to note 37 on p. 491, not a footnote here. 'Sc', 'Hn Harley 311', 'Ine bis Cnut' in the last paragraphs are roman. Sentence 'Hieraus collationirte ... Hn Harley 311 und copirte ... Additional 16278' rendered by sense (Harley 311 collated Hn from this; Additional 16278 copied Ine to Cnut).
proof_notes: text_en: last sentence reworded so that Harley 311 and Additional 16278 are the subjects, as in the German

wormald.shelfmark: London, British Library, Cotton MS Claudius D.ii
wormald.wormald_origin: Used by Andrew Horn when finalizing the texts in Co and Or; bequeathed by him to the Guildhall (p. 237); reconstructed with the other Liber Custumarum pieces by Ker (p. 237 n. 304)
wormald.laws: London collection version of Quadripartitus texts (see Table 4.7 'London' column)
wormald.laws_liebermann: Quadr, Ine, Blas, Forf, Hu, Af, AGu, App AGu, EGu, I As, As Alm, II As, Episc, Norðleod, Mirce, Að, Had, IV As, V As, III As, VI As, Ordal, I Cn, II Cn, Wl art retr, ECf retr, Lond ECf, Wl lad, CHn cor, Hn mon, Hn com, Hn, Hn Lond
wormald.other_contents: One of Horn's 'presentation copies' of the London collection, larger than Textus Roffensis (pp. 252–3); calligraphic (p. 239); two columns (p. 254).
wormald.overview: An early-fourteenth-century copy of the London collection, used by the London citizen Andrew Horn when settling the texts of his other copies and left by him to the Guildhall. Wormald counts it among Horn's large calligraphic presentation copies, written in two columns.
wormald.key_quote: represent various adaptations of the 'Leges Anglorum' to the purposes of the London businessman and worthy Andrew Horn (p. 238)
wormald.guide_shelfmark: London, British Library, Cotton MS Claudius D.ii (K2; once part of the London Guildhall’s Liber Custumarum)
verify_notes: Checked p. 237 (image: s xiv¹), 238–9, 252–4. Overview: 'one of the few calligraphic Quadripartitus witnesses' adjusted — Wormald says R and all the London-collection copies are calligraphic (p. 239); presentation-copy point given its source.

notes.text: Liebermann’s sigla (Gesetze I, p. xxxii): K2 for this MS, which in the London texts (Quadripartitus, Leges Henrici, Henry I’s London charter) he calls simply K; K3 for f. 41, a fifteenth-century addition copying Sc. Not to be confused with Cotton Claudius A.iii (K1, the previous entry), which Liebermann also calls K, for VI Æthelred and the coronation oath.
